## Definitions

- [statement] The same short-horizon study warns that its 183-pair panel is not 183 independent replications: it reports mean pairwise correlation of 0.40 and an effective count near 2.5. It also states that the original pairs were ranked by volume measured after the sample ended, leaving survivor-tilted membership. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21888 · keywords: Grid coin selection using recoverable oscillation and trading costs

## How it works

- [statement] Binance's Futures Grid FAQ gives a fee-adjusted geometric profit-per-grid formula and warns when profit per grid may not cover trading fees. The Dynamic Grid Trading paper uses a transaction fee of 0.0008 and reports lower profits from small grid sizes because fees consume a larger share of arbitrage profit; it also attributes poor IRR at large grid settings to infrequent activation. These are venue- and study-specific assumptions and findings. (medium confidence) — https://www.binance.com/en/support/faq/detail/f4c453bab89648beb722aa26634120c3 · keywords: Grid coin selection using recoverable oscillation and trading costs · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11921v1
- [statement] Bybit's spot-grid documentation distinguishes realized Grid Profit from Total P&L, which includes unrealized changes in the held base token. It explicitly states that Grid Profit can remain positive while Total P&L is negative when inventory losses exceed realized profits. (medium confidence) — https://www.bybit.com/en/help-center/article/FAQ-Spot-Grid-Bot · keywords: Grid coin selection using recoverable oscillation and trading costs · also: https://www.bybit.com/en/learn/bybit-trading-bot/spot-grid-bot-market-conditions
- [statement] Lipton and Lopez de Prado's abstract models oscillation using an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process and describes exits at a profit target, a maximum tolerated loss or a maximum holding horizon. It develops an analytical framework for profit-taking and stop-out levels by maximizing Sharpe ratio in that model. Leung and Li's abstract separately includes a stop-loss constraint in optimal entry and exit analysis. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.10502 · keywords: Grid coin selection using recoverable oscillation and trading costs · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.5062

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Two Binance Square community posts give different profit-per-grid rules of thumb: one suggests roughly 0.4% after fees, while another recommends net return per grid between 0.5% and 2%. These are attributed recommendations. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-08) — https://www.binance.com/en-ZA/square/post/381822568342127 · keywords: Grid coin selection using recoverable oscillation and trading costs · also: https://www.binance.com/en/square/post/383611508716720
- [statement] The Short-horizon mean reversion study reports significant directional reversal in 90% of 183 Binance pairs and a gross edge peaking near 1.3 bp per trade against a 5 bp benchmark round-trip cost. The reported experiment evaluates directional sign predictability, and its authors distinguish detectability from profitability at that benchmark cost. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21888 · keywords: Grid coin selection using recoverable oscillation and trading costs
- [statement] The Dynamic Grid Trading paper reports BTC and ETH backtests from January 2021 to July 2024 and attributes much of its reported peak 60–70% IRR performance to rising cryptocurrency prices. A Stevens Institute project separately reports that its machine-learning parameter variants did not outperform traditional grid methods. These are reported study results. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11921v1 · keywords: Grid coin selection using recoverable oscillation and trading costs · also: https://fsc.stevens.edu/cryptocurrency-market-making-improving-grid-trading-strategies-in-bitcoin/
- [statement] Bybit's Spot Grid FAQ states that initialization fails when estimated fill price deviates more than 10% from current market price, with the investment credited back. It separately describes failed initialization when slippage on the initial market buy leaves insufficient arbitrage opportunity or insufficient quote token to place the required orders. This is a venue-specific initialization safeguard. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-08) — https://www.bybit.com/en/help-center/article/FAQ-Spot-Grid-Bot · keywords: Grid coin selection using recoverable oscillation and trading costs

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] KuCoin warns that low liquidity can cause large slippage and a situation where a trader can buy but cannot sell. A Binance Square community guide similarly warns that thinly traded coins can gap through several grid lines at once. (medium confidence) — https://www.kucoin.com/support/20916860273561 · keywords: Grid coin selection using recoverable oscillation and trading costs · also: https://www.binance.com/en-ZA/square/post/381822568342127
- [statement] Binance's Futures Grid FAQ states that grid price differences cannot be below tick size and that each grid order must meet a minimum notional requirement. A Binance Square spot-grid guide separately notes that every grid line must meet the pair's minimum order size. These constraints depend on venue and product. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-08) — https://www.binance.com/en/support/faq/detail/f4c453bab89648beb722aa26634120c3 · keywords: Grid coin selection using recoverable oscillation and trading costs · also: https://www.binance.com/en-ZA/square/post/381822568342127
- [statement] Binance's Futures Grid FAQ includes realized profit, unrealized PnL and funding fees in total profit. A Binance Square futures-grid guide lists funding fees among contract-selection considerations and warns that leverage amplifies losses and can increase liquidation risk. These are futures-grid considerations. (medium confidence) — https://www.binance.com/en/support/faq/detail/f4c453bab89648beb722aa26634120c3 · keywords: Grid coin selection using recoverable oscillation and trading costs · also: https://www.binance.com/en-UZ/square/post/376851658061357
- [statement] OKX's Spot Grid documentation states that Trailing Down can extend the lower grid boundary when price continues falling. Each extension requires additional main-account capital; if funds are insufficient, the grid does not extend further. Its risk description warns of over-accumulating during a long bear market. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-08) — https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/whats-the-spot-grid-bot-and-how-to-use-it · keywords: Grid coin selection using recoverable oscillation and trading costs
- [statement] The abstract of the preprint Volatility Harvesting or Inventory Risk? reports positive average after-cost grid increments at three- and five-year horizons for Chinese equity ETFs relative to a static portfolio with the same initial exposure. It also reports limited historical signals and no stable out-of-sample spacing-selection advantage over fixed rules. These are abstract-reported results for equity ETFs. (low confidence) — https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=7429819 · keywords: Grid coin selection using recoverable oscillation and trading costs
- [statement] The HODL Strategy or Fantasy? abstract reports Monte Carlo simulations across 378 non-stablecoin crypto assets, net of trading fees and the opportunity cost of one-month Treasury bills. It reports a median excess return of -28.4 percent at a two-to-three-year horizon. Its separate prediction analysis reports economically negligible and unstable effects from endogenous predictors based on realized risk-return metrics. These are the paper's reported simulation and prediction results. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.02029 · keywords: Grid coin selection using recoverable oscillation and trading costs

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] KuCoin's spot-grid documentation prefers liquid pairs with two-sided price movement and explains that a one-sided market may keep buying or selling instead of completing repeated buy-low/sell-high cycles. Bitsgap likewise describes frequent swings within a range as suitable and persistent one-way movement as unsuitable. (high confidence) — https://www.kucoin.com/support/20916860273561 · keywords: Grid coin selection using recoverable oscillation and trading costs · also: https://bitsgap.com/blog/grid-trading-strategy-explained-how-to-profit-in-any-market-in-2026
- [statement] KuCoin's guidance prefers high liquidity and high volatility, whereas HaasOnline describes moderate volatility as suitable and advises avoiding volatility spikes. Bybit describes the tradeoff: wider swings can complete more grid trades, but swings large enough to exit the range halt execution. These are attributed qualitative guidelines. (medium confidence) — https://www.kucoin.com/support/20916860273561 · keywords: Grid coin selection using recoverable oscillation and trading costs · also: https://haasonline.com/grid-trading-bot, https://www.bybit.com/en/learn/bybit-trading-bot/spot-grid-bot-market-conditions
- [statement] Passivbot documents unilateralness as the absolute ratio of the exponential mean of completed one-minute log returns to the square root of their exponential mean square. It calls this directionality rather than absolute move magnitude. The documentation says implementation tests establish semantics and disabled-feature parity rather than profitability, and recommends assessing drawdown, exposure, underwater time, missed recoveries, fees and returns rather than fill counts alone. (low confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/enarjord/passivbot/master/docs/adaptive_entry_cooldown.md · keywords: Grid coin selection using recoverable oscillation and trading costs

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The Dynamic Grid Trading paper concludes that its finite grid has zero expected value under its stated equal-probability up/down price-step model, with no transaction fees and liquidation below the lower grid boundary. This is a conditional model result. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11921v1 · keywords: Grid coin selection using recoverable oscillation and trading costs
- [statement] KuCoin's example stops buying below the lower grid boundary and stops selling above the upper boundary. The Dynamic Grid Trading paper's reset variant retains cryptocurrency after a lower-bound break and uses arbitrage profits as principal for a new grid. The descriptions use different boundary rules. Bitsgap warns that a grid in a strong uptrend can sell too early and miss the continuation. (medium confidence) — https://www.kucoin.com/support/20916860273561 · keywords: Grid coin selection using recoverable oscillation and trading costs · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11921v1, https://bitsgap.com/blog/grid-trading-strategy-explained-how-to-profit-in-any-market-in-2026
- [statement] Bitsgap publishes a rule of thumb to inspect the last 30–60 days for a recognizable price range before launching a grid bot. A Binance Square guide describes AI settings that select a range and grid count from recent price history. These are setup heuristics described by the authors. (medium confidence) — https://bitsgap.com/blog/grid-trading-strategy-explained-how-to-profit-in-any-market-in-2026 · keywords: Grid coin selection using recoverable oscillation and trading costs · also: https://www.binance.com/en-ZA/square/post/381822568342127
- [statement] Passivbot's Forager documentation describes volume pruning followed by weighted ranking using quote volume, EMA entry readiness, volatility measured by a one-minute EMA of ln(high / low), and an optional unilateralness penalty for sustained one-way movement. Its configuration reference separately documents volume and volatility EMA inputs and score weights. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-08) — https://github.com/enarjord/passivbot/blob/master/docs/forager.md · keywords: Grid coin selection using recoverable oscillation and trading costs · also: https://github.com/enarjord/passivbot/blob/master/docs/configuration.md
- [statement] Martin and Schöneborn's abstract describes a no-trade buffer under linear transaction costs and a low-cost cube-root relation for its width. Leung and Li's abstract derives entry and exit intervals for an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck spread subject to transaction costs, with a stop-loss extension. These are results for their models. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1103.4934 · keywords: Grid coin selection using recoverable oscillation and trading costs · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.5062
- [statement] KuCoin states that USDT/USDC price fluctuations are small and therefore grid profits on that pair will be low. This is the exchange's description of a low-fluctuation pair. (low confidence) — https://www.kucoin.com/support/20916860273561 · keywords: Grid coin selection using recoverable oscillation and trading costs
- [statement] Freqtrade's plugin documentation describes VolatilityFilter as retaining a configured band between minimum and maximum historical volatility. It separately describes RangeStabilityFilter as removing pairs whose historical high-low range lies below or above configured bounds. These are software screening mechanisms. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-08) — https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/plugins/ · keywords: Grid coin selection using recoverable oscillation and trading costs
- [statement] Coinbase Learn describes grid trading as suitable for both trending and sideways markets. Bybit Learn says strongly one-directional markets are less suitable and describes execution stopping outside the range without an applicable trailing feature. The sources publish different qualitative suitability guidance. (medium confidence) — https://www.coinbase.com/learn/advanced-trading/what-is-a-grid-trading-bot-and-how-does-it-work · keywords: Grid coin selection using recoverable oscillation and trading costs · also: https://www.bybit.com/en/learn/bybit-trading-bot/spot-grid-bot-market-conditions
